saints.name: St. Francis of Paola
saints.title: Hermit and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A Calabrian hermit whose penance and miracles founded the Order of Minims, the “least” of religious…
biography: Born at Paola in Calabria on 27 March 1416 to poor parents who had begged a son through the intercession of Francis of Assisi, he spent a year among the Franciscans of San Marco Argentano and then, from 1432, lived alone as a hermit in a cave on the Tyrrhenian shore.

When two companions joined him about 1436, the order that would be called Minims began; Alexander VI later confirmed the rule and gave them that name, 'the least' in the household of God. To the usual vows Francis added a fourth, a perpetual Lenten abstinence from flesh, eggs, and dairy. He was never ordained a priest.

Renowned for prophecy and healing, he was summoned to France by the dying Louis XI and went only when the pope commanded. He prepared the king for death and remained at the French court as counsellor to Charles VIII and Louis XII.

He died at Plessis-les-Tours on Good Friday, 2 April 1507, and was canonized by Leo X in 1519. Because tradition holds that, refused passage by a boatman, he crossed the Strait of Messina on his spread cloak, Pius XII named him patron of the seafarers of Italy in 1943.
saints.knownFor: Founding the Order of Minims and a life of extreme penance.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 2 April
